## 固定收益開篇主論點

中東緊張情勢降溫，油價大幅下跌，在5月消費者物價報告公布前減輕了近期通膨預期壓力，帶動美國公債在6月9日上漲。這波行情暫時中斷、但沒有逆轉上週五強勁就業數據引發的重新定價。2年期殖利率下跌4.5個基點至4.119%，5年期與10年期均下降4.6個基點，分別收在4.245%與4.518%；30年期則下滑3.9個基點至4.998%。

各主要天期殖利率近乎平行移動，曲線變化有限。2年期與10年期利差僅收窄0.1個基點至39.9個基點，2年期與30年期利差則擴大0.6個基點至87.9個基點。10年期實質殖利率下跌2.9個基點至2.17%，損益兩平通膨率下降1.7個基點至2.348%，兩者均推動名目公債上漲：原油走弱降低了眼前的通膨溢價，風險偏好轉弱及CPI公布前的謹慎情緒，也壓低投資人持有長天期債券所要求的通膨調整後報酬。

伊朗與以色列停止最近一輪相互攻擊，圍繞更廣泛衝突的談判持續進行，WTI期貨下跌3.40%至$88.20，布蘭特原油下跌2.97%至$91.45。能源風險溢價下降，對正在判斷戰爭究竟只會造成短暫整體物價衝擊，還是會演變成迫使聯準會緊縮的廣泛通膨問題的利率市場而言，具有實質意義，但爭論並未就此落幕。原油價格仍高到足以影響近期通膨，美債曲線也明顯高於1個月前；期間2年期與10年期殖利率分別上升23.3與16.3個基點。

單日反彈也未動搖偏鷹部位。期貨定價顯示，市場預期聯準會年底前將完整升息25個基點；選擇權交易則押注9月會議前至少升息一次，甚至可能升息兩次。這種布局反映5月就業報告意外強勁，以及投資人擔心經濟活動韌性、能源成本與AI相關投資可能使現行政策的限制程度不足。6月10日公布的CPI將立即檢驗這些部位能否獲得進一步支持，或被迫回補空單。

美國財政部供給順利被市場吸收，未打斷債市回升。$580億的3年期公債標售殖利率為4.192%，遠高於5月的3.965%，但投標倍數由2.54升至2.64。間接與直接投標人合計取得84.72%的獲配競標量，一級交易商承接15.28%。這顯示重新定價後的殖利率吸引了終端投資人，即使市場仍在防範政策利率路徑上移。

整體收盤呈現利率壓力緩解、風險資產仍受抑制的格局。標普500指數下跌0.26%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.12%，費城半導體指數下挫1.93%；VIX則上升5.02%至19.87。美元指數下滑0.14%，黃金下跌1.75%，投資級、高收益與新興市場債券基金則都小幅收高。因此，美債同時獲得油價下跌與部分防禦性需求支持，但這並非資金全面逃離信用債，也不代表市場已明確放棄強勁成長的論述。

美國以外的政策反應更加強力，方向也更為分歧。印尼央行意外升息以捍衛印尼盾，但投資人聚焦財政干預與央行治理問題，當地公債仍持續遭到拋售。台灣則在資金緊俏與升息預期共同作用下，公債殖利率急升。日本方面，經濟學家幾乎一致預期日本央行下週緊縮，討論焦點已轉向第二次升息及未來縮減購債的速度。各市場面對的共同壓力都是通膨與匯率風險，但各國的政策可信度、流動性與財政選擇，決定了市場反應的差異。

## 油價回落暫緩美債重新定價

6月9日的反彈，是非農就業數據引發調整後，美債首次明顯喘息；但行情的組成反映的是壓力紓解，而非市場對緊縮看法全面投降。主要天期殖利率約下跌4至5個基點，扭轉前一交易日的升勢，30年期殖利率也回到略低於5%的水準。2年期殖利率仍高於聯準會3.5%至3.75%的目標區間，顯示市場依舊認為下一次具實質意義的政策調整更可能是緊縮，而不是寬鬆。

油價下跌是當日最直接的變化。布蘭特原油降至$91.45後，單週跌幅擴大至4.74%；WTI收在$88.20，同期下跌5.93%。伊朗與以色列停止相互攻擊，也在全球交易時段稍早提振工業金屬。倫敦銅價由跌轉升0.6%，反映緊張局勢緩和改善了全球需求的近期展望。跨市場反應同時把局勢降溫視為通膨壓力的喘息，以及嚴重經濟成長中斷風險的下降。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下跌與此解讀一致，但對名目美債漲幅的貢獻不到一半。實質殖利率同時下降2.9個基點，顯示在CPI公布前及科技股走弱之際，投資人也降低了所要求的實質利率補償。不過，拉長至1個月觀察，實質殖利率仍上升27.6個基點，損益兩平通膨率則下降11.3個基點。較大的趨勢仍指向市場上調對通膨調整後利率路徑的預期，而非長期通膨預期失去錨定。

這項區別對主席Kevin Warsh主持的首次FOMC會議尤其重要。10年期殖利率約4.5%，即使政策利率沒有立即上調，也會推高房貸與企業借款成本，對經濟形成限制。交易時段內引用的市場估算認為，近期殖利率升幅約相當於聯準會升息75個基點。然而，就業與投資依然強勁，促使投資人質疑這種金融條件收緊是否足以壓低需求，或經濟的中性利率是否已經上升。

因此，市場爭論已從下次何時調整利率，延伸至政策利率升到何種水準才不再刺激經濟。聯準會官員3月預測的長期利率中位數為3.1%；以交換市場估算的通膨調整後中性利率約為1.8%，高於決策官員對實質中性利率1.1%的中位估計。這些衡量方式不能直接等同於對下次會議的預測，但都反映市場懷疑目前的名目目標區間是否具有充分限制性。

AI投資是這場爭論的核心。部分投資人認為，資料中心及相關基礎設施建設在勞動市場仍具韌性之際形成新一波需求熱潮；未來雖可能提高生產力，眼前卻會增加支出與融資需求。另一些投資人只把經濟過熱視為風險情境，而非基準預測，仍在等待通膨數據與聯準會溝通提供更明確的證據。即使美債殖利率下跌，科技股當日仍走弱，顯示較高的必要報酬率，以及市場能否吸收龐大資本需求的疑問依舊重要。

選擇權市場展現的信念強於現貨債市漲勢。與擔保隔夜融資利率（SOFR）連結的合約中，部分交易結構可在9月中旬前至少升息一次、甚至兩次時獲利。非農就業數據公布後，選擇權交易量大增，期貨則反映2026年底前完整升息25個基點。避險基金在就業報告公布前持有創紀錄的SOFR期貨淨空單，但部分部位可能源自基差、避險或相對價值策略，不一定是直接的利率預測。

這種集中布局令市場對CPI呈現不對稱敏感度。若數據較溫和，近期升息理由將被削弱，部分偏空部位可能被迫縮減，進而放大美債漲勢；若通膨廣泛超出預期，則會證明避險布局合理，並鼓勵市場增加偏鷹交易。摩根大通客戶調查提供了溫和的相反訊號：最近一週直接放空美債的部位減少，投資人轉向中性部位，多單則維持不變。

殖利率下跌之際，現貨市場交易活動增加。FINRA記錄的美債面額交易量為$1.104兆，較6月8日增加14.2%；名目附息債交易量上升15.8%至$8,808億。剩餘期限超過2年至3年的附息債交易量大增66.2%至$1,609億，涵蓋最直接受到標售及政策重新定價影響的區段。7年至10年期區段成交量增加24.7%至$1,693億，超過3年至5年的區段則下降8.7%。

美國最新經濟數據不足以轉移市場對通膨的關注。4月商品與服務貿易逆差由修正後的$566億縮小至$559億，但仍略高於市場估計的$552億。出口增加$83億至$3,271億，進口增加$76億至$3,830億；商品逆差縮小$24億至$837億，服務順差則減少$17億至$278億。年度修訂改變了估算第二季成長所使用的基期，但淨額改善有限，未能動搖市場對物價與聯準會政策的聚焦。

## 升息避險加碼之際，標售需求仍穩

政策敏感型殖利率大幅上升後，3年期公債標售成為最清楚的實際需求測試。美國財政部以4.192%的最高得標殖利率發售$580億，較前次標售的3.965%高22.7個基點。發行規模維持不變，票息為4.125%，2029年6月15日到期，並於6月15日交割。

儘管利率環境走高，需求指標仍有改善。投標倍數由2.54升至2.64；間接投標人取得63.71%的獲配競標量，直接投標人取得21.01%，交易商承接比例降至15.28%。由於缺乏同期發行前交易殖利率作為參考，無法判定標售結果是出現尾差或低於發行前殖利率，但可以確認，這批對政策較敏感的供給獲得比5月更廣泛的參與。

標售順利被吸收，並不等於政策展望轉向。一場認購良好的標售可以在供給事件前後支撐市場，而不必與聯準會升息預期衝突。投資人獲得的殖利率遠高於1個月前，直接與間接投標人承接比例增加，顯示市場願意在重新定價後持有這批債券。因此，標售降低了眼前的供給壓力，但CPI與聯準會的反應函數仍是更重要的市場驅動因素。

國庫券標售結果較為分歧。$650.01億的42天期國庫券以3.600%的最高得標利率標出，低於前次的3.625%，投標倍數則由3.28微降至3.25；獲接受金額比上次標售少約$100億。間接投標人取得58.67%，直接投標人取得5.54%，交易商承接35.80%。該券於6月11日發行及交割，7月23日到期。

$500億的364天期國庫券以3.750%標出，比前次高10個基點，投標倍數由3.41降至3.34。間接投標比例升至68.23%，直接投標人取得2.19%，交易商承接29.59%。發行規模不變，6月11日交割，2027年6月10日到期。其較高的得標利率與較低投標倍數，和短天期國庫券的利率下降形成對比，反映前端各區段仍有差異，而非單一融資壓力事件。

3年期標售也為後續附息債供給建立基準。財政部將在6月10日CPI公布後續發$390億10年期公債，並於6月11日續發$220億30年期公債。相較3年期區段，這些天期受到下次聯準會會議的直接影響較小，對實質利率的不確定性、通膨持續性，以及投資人持有長天期部位所要求的補償更敏感。首場標售需求強勁是正面訊號，但不能預先決定較長天期債券的認購結果。

企業借款人面對同一套需求環境，結果卻因信用品質與交易結構而顯著分化。騰訊開始推銷美元與離岸人民幣債券；與投資人討論後，獲准籌資的上限提高至$45億，規模大於最初構想。10年期與20年期美元券的初步定價指引，分別約為美債殖利率加80與90個基點；擬發行的10年期及30年期人民幣債券，推銷殖利率則約為2.95%與3.55%。

截至週二上午，美元券訂單超過$30億，點心債訂單則突破人民幣205億元，約合$30億。北京擴大債券南向通計畫，允許特定保險公司增持離岸人民幣債券，也擴充了潛在需求池。募集資金預計用於再融資及一般用途，包括AI開發。騰訊有$35億債務與雙邊貸款將於2026年到期，另有$28億於2027年到期，但2026年並無公開發行的離岸債券到期。

Vedanta Resources籌備的交易則更明確以再融資為目的。公司聘請8家銀行規劃$52億再融資，涵蓋2028年至2033年到期的$36億債券，以及2028年起到期的$16億貸款。截至3月31日，公司淨負債已由5年前的$89億降至$49億；標普與穆迪也在5月調升其評等。

Vedanta希望把目前平均接近10%的融資成本最多降低300個基點。擬議方案可能納入5年、7年與10年期的攤還型債券，使本金得以逐步償還。針對尚未進入可贖回期的債券，公司計畫把回購價格訂在市價與全額補償價格之間。交易可望延長到期結構並降低再融資風險，但最終節省幅度取決於實際完成條件，不能只看公司公布的目標。

Shutterfly面對的投資人要求明顯更高。這家由Apollo支持的公司發行$11.5億垃圾債，殖利率達12%，並強化債權人保障，包括限制股利、投資，以及把資產移轉至債權人追索範圍之外；公司也限制以預期節省成本或一次性費用為基礎的獲利加回項目。儘管交易在預定6月10日定價前已獲超額認購，投資人仍反對進一步調降擬議殖利率。

這些讓步反映高槓桿，以及AI對個人化影像產品影響的不確定性。截至3月的3個月內，Shutterfly的EBITDA虧損由上年同期的$1,720萬擴大至$1,970萬，營收下降8%至$3.135億。調整後EBITDA則由虧損$150萬改善至約獲利$40萬；流動性總額為$4.74億，另有尚未動用的循環信用額度。3月底總負債達$24億，使這筆再融資除了必須提供雙位數殖利率，也有賴更嚴格的債權人保護。

整套融資還包括一筆$5億定期貸款，推銷條件為基準利率加650個基點、發行價格每1元面額96至97分，另有$2.25億第二順位留置權貸款。Shutterfly的獲利季節性依賴第四季，加上2023年一筆交易曾被穆迪歸類為困境債務交換，使契約文件格外重要。它與騰訊形成鮮明對比：充沛需求讓高品質發行人得以考慮擴大跨幣別交易，Shutterfly則必須支付高額溢酬並犧牲財務彈性。

CoreWeave也新增一筆可能進行的AI融資交易。這家資料中心營運商已安排與歐洲高收益債投資人通話，討論發行美元與歐元債券的可能性。公司獲穆迪評為Ba3、標普B+、惠譽BB-，已有美元債券流通，但尚未發行過歐元高收益債。在近期科技相關供給大多屬投資級債券的市場中，若發行歐元券，可為這家AI基礎設施借款人擴大投資人基礎。

## 亞洲市場考驗貨幣防衛的極限

印尼採取了當日最強力的政策行動。印尼央行在距例會尚有一週多之際意外升息25個基點，把BI-Rate調高至5.5%。此前印尼盾屢創歷史新低、股市重挫，外國投資人也日益擔憂總統普拉伯沃・蘇比安托帶有干預色彩的經濟政策。

這次升息之前，央行已於5月升息50個基點，幅度大於預期，使3週內累計緊縮幅度達75個基點。央行總裁Perry Warjiyo表示，最新行動旨在吸引外資流入，央行並承諾繼續干預匯市。這項防衛也付出代價：外匯存底在5月連續第5個月下降，是2018年以來最長的連跌期。

各類資產的初步反應明顯分歧。印尼盾從接近歷史低點的位置最多升值0.8%，創9個月最大漲幅；雅加達綜合指數盤中上漲約7%，由銀行股領漲。政府公債卻繼續下跌，10年期殖利率上升23個基點至7.51%，為2022年11月以來最高；5年期殖利率也升至2020年5月以來最高水準。

這種分歧顯示，提高政策利率可以暫時阻止匯率下跌，卻無法立即恢復市場對主權長天期債券的信心。印尼央行刻意推高當地殖利率，希望增加公債對外資的吸引力，但基金經理人仍擔心財政放寬、經濟治理與制度獨立性。交易員表示，央行先前曾在執行匯率操作時從次級市場買進公債，但6月8日並未進場。

國內政策發展加深了這些疑慮。國會議員擴大對央行的監督，並把央行職責延伸至經濟成長；普拉伯沃則任命自己的姪子進入央行領導層。新的大宗商品出口規定、貪腐調查，以及政府愈來愈直接的干預，都增加了不確定性。財政部與央行承諾加強協調，但投資人正在判斷，這種協調究竟會穩定政策，還是進一步模糊財政與貨幣職責的界線。

巴克萊、BNY與Mega Capital的分析師預期，印尼央行在6月18日例會還會升息，甚至可能再調高50個基點。較高利率可以提高印尼盾資產的相對報酬，但公債市場的反應顯示，投資人除了要求更高殖利率，也希望整體政策方向改變。即使週二反彈，印尼盾年初以來仍貶值近8%，印尼股市跌幅也仍超過30%。

台灣面臨的是另一種固定收益壓力。5年期公債殖利率大升32個基點至1.71%，創2008年11月以來最高；10年期公債標售殖利率則為2013年以來最高。季節性繳稅抽走銀行體系資金，壓縮可投入政府公債的資金；銀行為保留流動性，使流通在外可轉讓定期存單降至2014年以來最低。

資金趨緊之際，5月消費者通膨已升破警戒水準，市場也預期台灣央行將維持限制性政策。ING預測，若中東石油運輸再度受阻並推升能源價格，央行可能在第三季升息。澳盛銀行預期9月將一次性升息；若聯準會轉趨更鷹，行動時間可能提前。因此，公債賣壓是眼前流動性短缺與未來政策調整預期共同造成，而非單一因素所致。

日本的討論焦點已超越日本央行6月是否升息。在一項調查中，51名經濟學家有49人預期央行將於6月16日升息25個基點至約1%，為1995年以來最高水準。受訪者預期年底前利率將達1.25%，意味還會有第二次升息；71%預計之後大約每6個月調升一次。日本央行前理事早川英男另行評估，認為後續升息最早可能在10月。

隨油價上漲與國內財政支持增加，市場更加擔心日本央行落後於通膨情勢。60%的受訪經濟學家認為央行落後的風險正在上升，為這項問題納入調查以來最高比例。早川英男估計日本中性利率約為1.5%，但表示如果生活成本及企業轉嫁成本的力道持續強勁，政策利率最終可能需要升至約2%。

購債政策又增添一層複雜性。依現行計畫，日本央行每月購債額將在2027年4月開始的會計年度降至約¥2.1兆。調查中有44%預期央行停止縮減購債，36%預期放慢縮減速度，18%則認為目前每季減少¥2,000億的步調會持續。暫停縮減購債可能穩定長期殖利率，但也可能被解讀為配合政府財政方案，進而壓低日圓或削弱緊縮訊號。

日本政府同時試圖改變預算編列方式。財務大臣片山皋月把降低對補充預算依賴的努力，形容為日本戰後最大規模的預算改革。首相高市早苗希望把更多支出納入年度初始預算，以提高可預測性；不過，政府仍推出¥3.1兆追加方案，以因應通膨與伊朗衝突的影響。財務省沒有為該方案增加曆年公債發行額。

把經常性計畫移入初始預算，將使公共支出更容易追蹤，但也可能擴大本已約達¥122兆的起始預算。除非政府清楚區分項目重分類與新增支出，投資人起初可能把預算增加視為新一輪財政擴張。改革仍保留以補充預算因應不可預見事件的空間，因此執行與溝通比標題式承諾更為重要。

肯亞選擇維持利率，而非跟進緊縮。肯亞央行把基準利率維持在8.75%，符合全部6項預測；在上次會議前，央行曾連續降息10次，累計425個基點。5月年通膨率由5.6%加速至6.7%，核心通膨由2.8%升至3.2%。燃料壓力尤其嚴重，戰爭爆發以來柴油價格上漲40%，汽油上漲20%。

央行總裁Kamau Thugge預期，若衝突降溫，通膨仍會落在2.5%至7.5%的目標區間。肯亞先令保持穩定，$132億外匯存底足以支應將近6個月進口。央行把2026年經濟成長預測由5.3%下調至4.9%，並預期經常帳逆差將由2025年占GDP的2.1%擴大至3%。這次按兵不動，是在匯率受控與能源衝擊已推高通膨、削弱成長展望之間取得平衡。

## 歐洲成長與信用壓力令緊縮更棘手

德國4月工業生產增加0.4%，3月數據修正為下降0.1%；4月增幅略低於市場估計的0.5%。整體改善集中在成長2.4%的營建業；排除能源與營建的製造業產出持平，汽車產量則下降4.7%。總產出較上年同期減少0.5%，2月至4月也比前3個月低0.5%。

在歐洲央行6月11日會議前，這項數據的組成僅帶來有限安慰。營建業避免工業生產再度月減，但核心製造業停滯及汽車產量大降，顯示工業動能依然疲弱。此前製造業訂單已大幅下滑，進一步凸顯決策官員面臨的難題：能源價格正在推高通膨，基礎生產部門卻難以擴張。

法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin則提供了通膨面的新證據。他表示，伊朗戰爭造成的油價衝擊比先前假設更大、更持久，央行將上調法國2026年通膨預測。3月基準情境原先預估2026年通膨為1.7%、2027年為1.4%。法國經濟第一季意外萎縮，企業信心轉差，Moulin也表示新版展望將下調成長預測。

市場已完整反映歐洲央行2026年內再升息25個基點，並偏向預期還有第三次調升。6月決策料將把存款利率提高25個基點至2.25%。德國產出數據與Moulin更新預測，分別強化同一場爭論的兩面：經濟活動疲弱支持限制緊縮週期，持續性的能源衝擊則提高物價壓力由燃料擴散至其他領域的風險。

Moulin也主張，美國政策與聯準會獨立性的不確定性，為擴大歐元的國際角色帶來機會。他表示，歐洲需要更多以歐元計價的安全資產，並建議透過共同舉債為區域國防與AI計畫籌資。這類發行可擴大可投資歐元債券池，但共同舉債仍面臨強大政治阻力。因此，這項提議指出的是歐洲債券供給可能出現的結構性轉變，而非即將實施的融資決策。

流動性較差的歐洲信用市場已可見壓力。對高槓桿光纖網路營運商有曝險的銀行，開始折價出售貸款給困境債務投資人。德國DNS:Net的贊助股東3i Infrastructure拒絕再注資，並把股權價值減記至零後，FitzWalter Capital買下該公司約一半的銀行債務。Strategic Value Partners則在Deutsche Glasfaser進行€70億重組期間，收購約€3.5億貸款。

2021年至2024年間，歐洲光纖業者為建設相互競爭的網路而大量舉債，吸引約€850億債務融資。客戶連線數與現金流未能跟上建設速度，德國與英國尤其明顯；利息與營運成本上升也破壞了再融資計畫。AlixPartners估計，約65%的歐洲光纖公司必須在2年內完成再融資。

Deutsche Glasfaser的重組要求贊助股東提供€8.45億特別股資本，貸款人則把€17億債務置於次順位，並供應€4億新融資。英國業者CityFibre完成一輪由貸款人及股東投入£23億的資本重整後，可能仍需要約£10億支應成長。即使營運公司尚未進入正式破產程序，把貸款移轉給困境債務基金，也代表債權人結構與談判關係已經改變。

塞內加爾的主權債務壓力仍十分嚴峻。標普維持該國CCC+長期外幣評等的負向展望，並警告若無法取得新的IMF計畫，市場對融資的疑慮將加劇。2024年發現隱藏債務後，原有的$18億融資安排遭到暫停；IMF工作團隊預定下週訪問達卡。

標普估計，塞內加爾的融資需求約相當於GDP的30%。該國2031年到期美元債券6月8日殖利率達24.56%，追平歷史紀錄；主權債相對美債利差則超過1,500個基點。被排除在國際市場之外，使塞內加爾更加依賴區域融資，也提高風險經西非銀行向外擴散的可能性。國內投資人持有約73%的本地債務，存款支撐的銀行流動性仍能維持需求，但這些緩衝無法取代IMF協議可能協助恢復的外部融資管道。

## 前瞻市場意涵

美東時間6月10日08:30公布的5月CPI，是檢驗美債漲勢與市場新緊縮傾向的即時關卡。整體通膨預計月增0.5%、年增4.2%，前值分別為0.6%與3.8%；核心通膨月增率預計由0.4%降至0.2%，年增率則由2.8%升至2.9%。關鍵在於能源是否仍是主要推力，或物價壓力已擴散至核心商品與服務。

若核心數據較溫和，押注聯準會提早升息的選擇權部位將受到挑戰，龐大的期貨空頭曝險也可能被迫回補。若核心通膨廣泛上升或加速，則會支持另一種判斷：即使油價回落，強韌的就業與投資仍需要更緊的政策。10年期殖利率的組成變化容許市場向任何一方反應，因為實質殖利率過去1個月仍明顯上升，損益兩平通膨率則已下降。

CPI公布後，美國財政部將於美東時間13:00續發$390億10年期公債。該券票息4.375%，2036年5月15日到期，6月15日交割。通膨結果重新調整殖利率後，標售將檢驗3年期公債所見的強勁終端投資人需求能否延伸至長天期部位，也會區分市場對政策敏感型公債的需求，與對承受長期實質利率及通膨展望風險債券的需求。

歐洲央行將於美東時間6月11日08:15公布決策，市場主流預期存款利率升息25個基點至2.25%。新的預測與政策指引，將決定這次行動被描述為防範能源成本轉嫁的有限措施，還是更長緊縮序列的一部分。德國核心製造業停滯，以及法國成長走弱、預期通膨上升的組合，使這項區別對德國公債及其他歐洲殖利率曲線格外重要。

美國生產者物價與初領失業救濟金人數將在同日美東時間08:30公布。5月最終需求PPI預計上升0.7%，核心指標上升0.5%，前值經修正後分別增加1.4%與1.0%。初領失業救濟金人數前值為22.5萬人，創4個月高點。兩項數據合併觀察，可判斷上游通膨是否正在擴散，以及勞動市場是否仍強到足以承受更多政策限制。

財政部隨後將於6月11日美東時間13:00續發$220億30年期公債，票息為5.000%，6月15日交割。3年期、10年期與30年期公債將在當日形成$1,190億附息債總交割額，時間就在6月16日至17日FOMC會議之前。CPI、PPI及歐洲央行決策公布後，長債標售將檢驗投資人是否重新要求發行讓利，尤其30年期殖利率仍徘徊在5%左右。

日本央行6月16日決策是亞洲長天期債市的主要事件。市場幾乎一致預期升息25個基點至約1%，但有關第二次升息與縮減購債速度的指引，重要性將超過首次行動本身。若央行明確承諾進一步正常化，將支持市場對年底利率達1.25%的預期；若放慢縮減購債，雖可能抑制日本公債波動，卻也會引發緊縮訊號是否一致的疑問。

印尼央行6月18日例會則將檢驗，意外升息究竟是一次性干預，還是更大規模防衛行動的開端。分析師已提出再次升息50個基點的可能性。關鍵證據是印尼盾反彈能否持續，以及政府公債殖利率能否穩定。若進一步緊縮仍無法改善長天期公債表現，將更支持外資撤退是由制度與財政疑慮驅動，而非單純因利息收益不足的判斷。

overall_summary.headline: 油價回落暫緩非農就業後的重新定價，美債反彈
overall_summary.session_narrative:
伊朗與以色列停止最近一輪相互攻擊，WTI下跌3.40%至$88.20，布蘭特原油下跌2.97%至$91.45，帶動美債在6月9日上漲。2年期殖利率下跌4.5個基點至4.119%，10年期下降4.6個基點至4.518%，30年期下滑3.9個基點至4.998%。10年期實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率雙雙下降，顯示油價走低及實質利率補償減少都推動了行情。

這波漲勢只是暫緩、而非逆轉強勁5月就業數據後的重新定價。期貨仍反映年底前完整升息25個基點，選擇權則押注9月中旬前升息一次，甚至可能兩次。6月10日公布的5月CPI將檢驗能源壓力減弱是否足以抑制通膨，或強韌需求是否正在擴大物價漲勢。

財政部$580億3年期公債雖以4.192%標出，參與情況仍優於5月，投標倍數升至2.64，交易商承接比例僅15.28%。科技股領跌、波動率上升，顯示風險資產仍受抑制，但投資級、高收益與新興市場債券基金均小幅收高。亞洲方面，印尼意外升息雖支撐印尼盾，卻未能阻止主權債遭到拋售，凸顯單靠提高利息收益仍不足以化解財政與制度疑慮。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on June 9 as easing Middle East tensions pushed oil sharply lower, taking some immediate pressure off inflation expectations before the May consumer-price report. The move interrupted, but did not reverse, the repricing that followed Friday’s strong employment data. The 2-year yield fell 4.5 basis points to 4.119%, the 5-year and 10-year each declined 4.6 basis points to 4.245% and 4.518%, and the 30-year eased 3.9 basis points to 4.998%.

The nearly parallel move left the curve largely unchanged. The 2s10s spread narrowed just 0.1 basis point to 39.9 basis points, while 2s30s steepened 0.6 basis point to 87.9 basis points. At 10 years, the real yield fell 2.9 basis points to 2.17% and breakeven inflation declined 1.7 basis points to 2.348%. Both components therefore contributed to the rally: weaker crude reduced the immediate inflation premium, while softer risk appetite and pre-CPI caution lowered the inflation-adjusted return demanded on duration.

WTI futures fell 3.40% to $88.20 and Brent declined 2.97% to $91.45 after Iran and Israel halted their latest exchange of strikes and negotiations over the wider conflict continued. The reduction in the energy risk premium was meaningful for a rates market debating whether the war will produce a temporary headline-price shock or a broader inflation problem requiring Federal Reserve tightening. It did not settle that question. Crude remained high enough to affect near-term inflation, and the Treasury curve still stood materially above its levels a month earlier, with the 2-year yield up 23.3 basis points and the 10-year up 16.3 basis points over that period.

Hawkish positioning also survived the daily rally. Futures were pricing a full quarter-point Fed increase by year-end, while options trades targeted one or possibly two moves by the September meeting. That stance reflected the unexpectedly strong May employment report and concern that resilient activity, energy costs and AI-related investment could leave current policy insufficiently restrictive. CPI on June 10 became the immediate test of whether those positions would gain further support or face short covering.

Treasury supply was absorbed without disrupting the recovery. The $58 billion 3-year auction cleared at 4.192%, sharply above May’s 3.965%, but its 2.64 bid-to-cover ratio improved from 2.54. Indirect and direct bidders together took 84.72% of accepted competitive tenders, leaving primary dealers with 15.28%. The result showed that the repriced yield attracted end-user demand even as investors continued to protect against a higher policy path.

The broader close combined rate relief with restraint in risk assets. The S&P 500 slipped 0.26%, the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.12% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index lost 1.93%, while the VIX rose 5.02% to 19.87. The dollar index eased 0.14% and gold fell 1.75%. Investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt funds all finished modestly higher. Treasuries were therefore supported by lower oil and some defensive demand, but the session did not amount to a wholesale flight from credit or a decisive retreat from the strong-growth narrative.

Outside the U.S., policy responses became more forceful and more divergent. Bank Indonesia delivered an unscheduled rate increase to defend the rupiah, yet local bonds continued to sell off as investors focused on fiscal intervention and central-bank governance. Taiwan’s government-bond yields surged under a combination of tight cash and expectations of a policy increase. In Japan, economists overwhelmingly expected the Bank of Japan to tighten next week, while debate shifted toward a second move and the future pace of bond-purchase reductions. The common pressure was inflation and currency risk, but domestic credibility, liquidity and fiscal choices determined how each market reacted.

## Oil Relief Interrupts the Treasury Repricing

The June 9 rally gave Treasuries their first clear respite after the payroll-driven adjustment, but its composition showed relief rather than capitulation. Yields fell by roughly 4 to 5 basis points across the main maturities, reversing the previous session’s increase and returning the 30-year yield just below 5%. The 2-year remained above the Fed’s 3.5% to 3.75% target range, preserving the market’s judgment that the next meaningful policy adjustment is more likely to be tighter than easier.

Lower oil supplied the most direct daily change. Brent’s decline to $91.45 extended its weekly fall to 4.74%, while WTI’s close at $88.20 left it 5.93% lower over the same period. Industrial metals also benefited earlier in the global session from the halt in Iran-Israel strikes: copper rose 0.6% in London after initially falling, as easing tensions improved the immediate outlook for global demand. The cross-market response treated de-escalation as both an inflation reprieve and a reduction in the risk of a severe growth interruption.

The drop in the 10-year breakeven was consistent with that interpretation, though it accounted for less than half of the nominal Treasury rally. The simultaneous 2.9-basis-point decline in the real yield showed that investors also marked down the real-rate compensation required before CPI and amid weakness in technology shares. Over one month, however, the real yield remained 27.6 basis points higher while the breakeven was 11.3 basis points lower. The larger trend continued to reflect a higher expected path for inflation-adjusted rates, not an unanchored long-term inflation outlook.

That distinction matters for Chairman Kevin Warsh’s first FOMC meeting. A 10-year yield around 4.5% raises mortgage and corporate borrowing costs and imposes restraint without an immediate increase in the policy rate. Market estimates cited during the session equated the recent yield rise to roughly 75 basis points of Fed tightening. Yet the strength of employment and investment has prompted investors to question whether that financial restraint is enough to cool demand or whether the economy’s neutral rate has moved higher.

The market debate has consequently broadened from the date of the next move to the level at which policy stops stimulating activity. The median longer-run rate in Fed officials’ March projections was 3.1%, while a swaps-based estimate of the inflation-adjusted neutral rate was around 1.8%, compared with a 1.1% median real estimate from policymakers. Those measures are not directly equivalent to a forecast for the next meeting, but both point to skepticism that the current nominal target range is substantially restrictive.

AI investment is central to the argument. Some investors see the build-out of data centers and related infrastructure as a demand boom arriving while the labor market remains resilient, potentially lifting productivity later but adding to spending and financing needs now. Others regard overheating as a risk scenario rather than the base case and are waiting for clearer evidence from inflation and the Fed’s communication. The daily fall in technology shares showed that higher required returns and questions about capital absorption remain relevant even when Treasury yields decline.

The options market displayed more conviction than the cash rally. Trading in contracts linked to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate included structures that would gain from at least one increase and potentially two by mid-September. Options activity had surged after payrolls, and futures priced a full 25-basis-point increase by the end of 2026. Hedge funds had entered the payroll release with a record net short position in SOFR futures, although some of that exposure may reflect basis, hedging or relative-value strategies rather than a direct rate forecast.

That concentration creates asymmetric sensitivity to CPI. A softer result could weaken the near-term case for tightening and force bearish positions to be reduced, amplifying a Treasury rally. A broad inflation surprise would validate the protection and encourage additional hawkish trades. A JPMorgan client survey offered a modest counterpoint: outright Treasury shorts declined during the latest week, with investors shifting toward neutral positions while longs were unchanged.

Cash-market activity increased as yields fell. FINRA recorded $1.104 trillion of Treasury par activity, 14.2% more than on June 8, while nominal-coupon activity rose 15.8% to $880.8 billion. Activity in coupons with more than 2 and up to 3 years remaining jumped 66.2% to $160.9 billion, encompassing the sector most directly affected by the auction and policy repricing. Turnover in the 7- to 10-year sector increased 24.7% to $169.3 billion, while activity above 3 and through 5 years declined 8.7%.

Fresh U.S. economic evidence was not strong enough to displace the inflation debate. The goods-and-services trade deficit narrowed to $55.9 billion in April from a revised $56.6 billion, slightly wider than the $55.2 billion estimate. Exports rose $8.3 billion to $327.1 billion and imports increased $7.6 billion to $383 billion. The goods deficit narrowed $2.4 billion to $83.7 billion, while the services surplus shrank $1.7 billion to $27.8 billion. Annual revisions changed the base used for second-quarter growth estimates, but the modest net improvement did not challenge the market’s focus on prices and Fed policy.

## Auction Demand Holds as Hike Hedges Build

The 3-year auction provided the clearest realized test of demand after the sharp rise in policy-sensitive yields. Treasury sold $58 billion at a 4.192% high yield, 22.7 basis points above the previous auction’s 3.965%. The offering size was unchanged, and the securities carry a 4-1/8% coupon, mature on June 15, 2029, and settle on June 15.

Demand measures improved despite the higher rate environment. The bid-to-cover ratio rose to 2.64 from 2.54. Indirect bidders took 63.71% of accepted competitive tenders and direct bidders received 21.01%, while the dealer share fell to 15.28%. Without a contemporaneous when-issued reference, the result does not establish whether the auction tailed or stopped through. It does show that the policy-sensitive supply found stronger broad participation than in May.

The distinction between auction absorption and the policy outlook is important. A well-covered sale can support the market around the supply event without contradicting expectations for Fed increases. Investors were offered a substantially higher yield than a month earlier, and the larger direct and indirect takedown indicated willingness to own the notes at that reset level. The auction therefore reduced immediate supply pressure while leaving CPI and the Fed reaction function as the larger drivers.

Bill results were more mixed. The $65.001 billion 42-day auction stopped at a 3.600% high rate, down from 3.625% previously, with bid-to-cover edging down to 3.25 from 3.28. The accepted amount was about $10 billion smaller than at the prior auction. Indirect bidders took 58.67%, direct bidders 5.54% and dealers 35.80%. The bill is issued and settles on June 11 and matures on July 23.

The $50 billion 364-day auction cleared at 3.750%, 10 basis points above the previous sale, while bid-to-cover softened to 3.34 from 3.41. Indirect participation increased to 68.23%, direct bidders took 2.19% and dealers received 29.59%. The unchanged-size issue settles June 11 and matures June 10, 2027. The higher clearing rate and lower cover contrasted with the shorter bill’s lower rate, preserving differentiation across the front end rather than signaling a single funding-stress event.

The 3-year result also set a benchmark for the rest of the coupon sequence. Treasury will reopen $39 billion of 10-year notes after CPI on June 10 and $22 billion of 30-year bonds on June 11. Those maturities are exposed less directly to the next Fed meeting than the 3-year sector and more to real-rate uncertainty, inflation persistence and the amount of compensation investors require for duration. Strong demand in the first sale is constructive, but it does not predetermine the reception at longer maturities.

Corporate borrowers faced the same demand environment with sharply different outcomes depending on credit quality and structure. Tencent began marketing dollar and offshore-yuan bonds in a deal authorized to raise as much as $4.5 billion, larger than initially contemplated after discussions with investors. Initial guidance was around 80 basis points over Treasuries for a 10-year dollar tranche and 90 basis points for a 20-year tranche. The proposed 10-year and 30-year yuan notes were marketed around 2.95% and 3.55%.

Orders exceeded $3 billion for the dollar portions by mid-morning Tuesday and topped 20.5 billion yuan, also about $3 billion, for the dim sum tranches. Beijing’s decision to let selected insurers buy more offshore-yuan bonds through an expanded southbound program helped deepen the potential demand pool. Proceeds were expected to support refinancing and general purposes, including AI development. Tencent had $3.5 billion of debt and bilateral loans maturing in 2026 and $2.8 billion due in 2027, though it had no public offshore bonds maturing during 2026.

Vedanta Resources was preparing a much more explicitly refinancing-driven transaction. The company hired eight banks for a planned $5.2 billion refinancing covering $3.6 billion of bonds maturing from 2028 through 2033 and $1.6 billion of loans due from 2028 onward. Its net debt had fallen to $4.9 billion as of March 31 from $8.9 billion five years earlier, and S&P and Moody’s upgraded the company in May.

Vedanta was targeting as much as a 300-basis-point reduction in funding costs from an average near 10%. The proposed package may include amortizing bonds with 5-, 7- and 10-year maturities, allowing principal to be repaid gradually. For bonds not yet callable, the company planned repurchase prices between market value and make-whole value. The transaction would extend maturities and reduce refinancing risk, but the final savings depend on execution rather than the announced target alone.

Shutterfly encountered a more demanding investor response. The Apollo-backed company strengthened protections on a $1.15 billion junk-bond offering carrying a 12% yield by restricting dividends, investments and transfers of assets beyond creditors’ reach. It also limited the use of earnings add-backs based on prospective savings or one-time costs. Investors had resisted any tightening of the proposed yield, even though the deal was oversubscribed ahead of expected pricing on June 10.

The concessions reflected both leverage and uncertainty about AI’s effect on personalized-image products. Shutterfly reported an EBITDA loss of $19.7 million for the 3 months through March, wider than $17.2 million a year earlier, while revenue fell 8% to $313.5 million. Adjusted EBITDA improved to about $400,000 from a $1.5 million loss, and liquidity totaled $474 million with an undrawn revolver. Total debt stood at $2.4 billion at the end of March, leaving the refinancing dependent on creditor protections as well as a double-digit yield.

The package also included a $500 million term loan marketed at 650 basis points over its benchmark and an issue price of 96 to 97 cents, plus a $225 million second-lien loan. Shutterfly’s seasonal reliance on fourth-quarter earnings and its history of a 2023 transaction classified by Moody’s as a distressed exchange increased the importance of documentation. The contrast with Tencent was stark: abundant demand allowed a high-quality issuer to consider a larger deal across currencies, while Shutterfly had to pay a steep premium and surrender flexibility.

CoreWeave added another prospective AI-financing transaction. The data-center operator scheduled calls with European high-yield investors to discuss possible dollar and euro bonds. Rated Ba3 by Moody’s, B+ by S&P and BB- by Fitch, it already has dollar bonds outstanding but has not issued euro high-yield notes. A euro transaction would broaden the investor base for an AI infrastructure borrower in a market where most recent technology-related supply has been investment grade.

## Asian Markets Test the Limits of Monetary Defense

Indonesia delivered the session’s most forceful policy action. Bank Indonesia raised the BI-Rate 25 basis points to 5.5% in an unscheduled decision, more than a week before its regular meeting. The move followed repeated record lows in the rupiah, a deep equity decline and accelerating foreign concern about President Prabowo Subianto’s interventionist economic program.

The increase brought cumulative tightening to 75 basis points in 3 weeks, following a larger-than-expected 50-basis-point move in May. Governor Perry Warjiyo said the latest action was intended to attract foreign inflows, and the central bank pledged continued currency intervention. That defense has come at a cost: foreign-exchange reserves declined for a fifth consecutive month in May, the longest losing streak since 2018.

The initial response split sharply across assets. The rupiah strengthened as much as 0.8% from near a record low, its largest gain in 9 months, and the Jakarta Composite rose about 7% intraday, led by banks. Government bonds continued to fall. The 10-year yield climbed 23 basis points to 7.51%, its highest since November 2022, while the 5-year yield reached its highest level since May 2020.

The divergence showed that a higher policy rate could interrupt the currency decline without immediately restoring confidence in sovereign duration. Bank Indonesia was deliberately seeking higher local yields to make bonds more attractive to foreign investors, but fund managers remained concerned about fiscal loosening, economic management and institutional independence. The central bank had bought bonds in the secondary market as part of its currency operations but was absent on June 8, according to traders.

Domestic policy developments intensified those concerns. Lawmakers expanded parliamentary supervision of the central bank and broadened its mandate to include growth, while Prabowo appointed his nephew to the bank’s leadership. New commodity-export rules, a corruption investigation and increasingly direct government intervention added to uncertainty. The finance ministry and central bank promised closer coordination, but investors were assessing whether that alignment would stabilize policy or further blur fiscal and monetary responsibilities.

Analysts at Barclays, BNY and Mega Capital expected another increase at the scheduled June 18 meeting, with a further 50-basis-point move considered possible. Higher rates can improve the relative return on rupiah assets, but the bond-market response indicated that investors wanted changes in the broader policy direction as well as more yield. The rupiah remained nearly 8% weaker for the year and Indonesian equities were still down more than 30%, despite Tuesday’s rebound.

Taiwan experienced a different form of fixed-income stress. The 5-year government yield jumped 32 basis points to 1.71%, its highest since November 2008, and a 10-year auction produced the highest yield since 2013. Seasonal tax payments drained banking-system cash, reducing the funds available for government bonds. Outstanding negotiable certificates of deposit fell to the lowest level since 2014 as lenders preserved liquidity.

Tighter cash coincided with expectations that Taiwan’s central bank would keep policy restrictive after consumer inflation moved above its alert level in May. ING projected a rate increase in Q3 if renewed disruption to Middle East oil flows lifted energy prices. ANZ expected a one-off increase in September, with an earlier move possible if the Fed adopted a more hawkish stance. The selloff therefore combined an immediate liquidity shortage with a prospective policy adjustment, rather than reflecting either force alone.

Japan’s debate moved beyond whether the BOJ will tighten in June. In a survey, 49 of 51 economists expected a 25-basis-point increase to around 1% on June 16, the highest rate since 1995. Respondents expected the rate to reach 1.25% by year-end, implying a second move, and 71% anticipated increases at a pace of roughly once every 6 months. A separate assessment from former BOJ Executive Director Hideo Hayakawa identified October as the earliest likely date for the follow-up.

Concern that the BOJ is behind the inflation curve has increased alongside oil prices and domestic fiscal support. Sixty percent of surveyed economists saw a rising risk of the bank falling behind, the highest share since the question was introduced. Hayakawa estimated Japan’s neutral rate at about 1.5% but said the policy rate might ultimately need to reach around 2% if living costs and corporate pass-through remain strong.

Bond purchases add a separate complication. Under the current plan, monthly BOJ buying is scheduled to fall to about ¥2.1 trillion in the fiscal year starting April 2027. In the survey, 44% expected the bank to stop reducing purchases, 36% expected it to slow the reductions and 18% expected the current ¥200 billion-per-quarter pace to continue. A pause could stabilize long yields, but it could also be interpreted as accommodating the government’s fiscal program, potentially weakening the yen or undermining the tightening message.

The government is simultaneously trying to change how it budgets. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama described the effort to reduce reliance on supplementary budgets as Japan’s largest postwar budget reform. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi wants more spending incorporated into the initial annual budget to improve predictability, although the government still introduced a ¥3.1 trillion extra package to address inflation and consequences of the Iran conflict. The ministry avoided adding to calendar-year bond issuance to finance that package.

Moving recurring programs into the initial budget would make public spending easier to track, but it could enlarge a starting budget that already totals about ¥122 trillion. Investors may initially perceive the increase as new fiscal expansion unless the government clearly separates reclassification from additional spending. The reform also retains supplementary budgets for unforeseen events, leaving implementation and communication more important than the headline commitment.

Kenya chose to hold rather than tighten. Its central bank left the benchmark rate at 8.75%, matching all 6 forecasts, after 10 consecutive reductions totaling 425 basis points before the previous meeting. Annual inflation accelerated to 6.7% in May from 5.6%, while core inflation rose to 3.2% from 2.8%. Fuel pressure was severe: diesel prices had increased 40% and gasoline 20% since the war began.

Governor Kamau Thugge expected inflation to remain within the 2.5% to 7.5% target band if the conflict de-escalated. The shilling was stable, and $13.2 billion in reserves covered almost 6 months of imports. The central bank lowered its 2026 growth projection to 4.9% from 5.3% and expected the current-account deficit to widen to 3% of GDP from 2.1% in 2025. The hold balanced a contained currency against an energy shock already lifting inflation and weakening the growth outlook.

## European Growth and Credit Stress Complicate Tightening

German industrial production rose 0.4% in April after a revised 0.1% decline in March, narrowly missing the 0.5% estimate. The headline improvement was concentrated in construction, which increased 2.4%. Manufacturing excluding energy and construction was unchanged, while automotive production fell 4.7%. Output was 0.5% lower than a year earlier and also down 0.5% in February through April compared with the preceding 3 months.

The composition offered only limited reassurance before the ECB’s June 11 meeting. Construction prevented another monthly decline, but flat core manufacturing and a sharp fall in autos showed that industrial momentum remained weak. That evidence followed a large drop in manufacturing orders and reinforced the problem facing policymakers: energy is raising inflation while the underlying production base is struggling to expand.

Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin supplied fresh evidence on the inflation side. He said the central bank would raise its 2026 French inflation forecast because the Iran war had made the oil shock larger and more persistent than previously assumed. The March baseline had projected inflation of 1.7% in 2026 and 1.4% in 2027. Moulin also said the new outlook would show weaker growth, after France’s economy unexpectedly contracted in Q1 and business confidence deteriorated.

Markets were fully pricing another quarter-point ECB increase during 2026 and leaning toward a third move. The June decision was expected to lift the deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.25%. German output and Moulin’s forecast update strengthened opposite sides of the same argument: weak activity favors limiting the tightening cycle, while a persistent energy shock increases the risk that price pressure spreads beyond fuel.

Moulin also argued that uncertainty about U.S. policy and Fed independence created an opportunity to expand the euro’s international role. He said Europe would need more safe assets denominated in euros and suggested common borrowing for regional defense and AI projects. Such issuance would deepen the pool of investable euro debt, but political resistance to joint borrowing remains substantial. The proposal therefore identified a possible structural shift in European supply rather than an imminent financing decision.

Stress was already visible in less liquid European credit. Banks exposed to highly leveraged fiber-network operators have begun selling loans at discounts to distressed-debt investors. FitzWalter Capital bought about half of the bank debt of Germany’s DNS:Net after sponsor 3i Infrastructure declined to inject more money and wrote its equity stake down to zero. Strategic Value Partners acquired roughly €350 million of Deutsche Glasfaser loans during a €7 billion restructuring.

The sector borrowed heavily between 2021 and 2024 to build competing fiber networks, attracting about €85 billion of debt financing. Customer connections and cash flow failed to keep pace with construction, particularly in Germany and the U.K., while higher interest and operating costs undermined refinancing plans. AlixPartners estimated that about 65% of European fiber companies must refinance within 2 years.

Deutsche Glasfaser’s restructuring required sponsors to provide €845 million of preferred equity, while lenders subordinated €1.7 billion of debt and supplied €400 million of new financing. U.K. provider CityFibre may need about £1 billion more to fund growth after a recapitalization that already brought £2.3 billion from lenders and shareholders. The transfer of loans to distressed funds marks a change in creditor ownership and bargaining dynamics, even where operating companies have not entered formal insolvency.

Sovereign distress remained acute in Senegal. S&P maintained a negative outlook on the country’s CCC+ long-term foreign-currency rating and warned that failure to secure a new IMF program would intensify concern about financing. An IMF staff mission is scheduled to visit Dakar next week after a prior $1.8 billion facility was suspended in 2024 following the discovery of hidden debt.

Senegal’s financing needs amount to roughly 30% of GDP, according to S&P. Its dollar bond due in 2031 yielded 24.56% on June 8, matching a record, while the sovereign spread exceeded 1,500 basis points over Treasuries. Exclusion from international markets has increased reliance on regional financing and raised potential spillover risks through West African banks. Domestic investors hold about 73% of local debt, and deposit-supported bank liquidity continues to sustain demand, but those buffers do not replace the external funding access that an IMF agreement could help restore.

## Forward Market Significance

May CPI at 08:30 ET on June 10 is the immediate test of the Treasury rally and the market’s new tightening bias. Headline inflation is expected to rise 0.5% on the month and 4.2% from a year earlier, following 0.6% and 3.8%. Core inflation is expected to slow to 0.2% monthly from 0.4% while increasing to 2.9% annually from 2.8%. The key distinction is whether energy remains the dominant impulse or whether price pressure broadens through core goods and services.

A softer core result would challenge options positions targeting early Fed increases and could force some of the large bearish futures exposure to unwind. Broad or accelerating core inflation would support the judgment that resilient employment and investment require tighter policy even if oil retreats. The 10-year decomposition leaves room for either response: real yields remain substantially higher over the month, while breakevens have declined.

Treasury will reopen $39 billion of 10-year notes at 13:00 ET after CPI. The securities carry a 4.375% coupon, mature May 15, 2036, and settle June 15. The auction will test whether the strong end-user participation seen in the 3-year sale extends to duration once the inflation result has reset yields. It will also separate demand for policy-sensitive notes from demand for bonds exposed to the longer-run real-rate and inflation outlook.

The ECB decides at 08:15 ET on June 11, with a 25-basis-point increase in the deposit rate to 2.25% forming the prevailing expectation. New projections and guidance will determine whether the move is presented as limited protection against energy pass-through or part of a longer sequence. Germany’s flat manufacturing core and France’s combination of weaker growth and higher expected inflation make that distinction consequential for Bunds and other European curves.

U.S. producer prices and initial claims arrive at 08:30 ET the same day. Final-demand PPI is expected to rise 0.7% in May and the core measure 0.5%, following revised gains of 1.4% and 1.0%. Claims follow a 225,000 reading that reached a 4-month high. Together, the releases will show whether pipeline inflation is broadening while the labor market remains strong enough to tolerate additional restraint.

Treasury then reopens $22 billion of 30-year bonds at 13:00 ET on June 11. The securities carry a 5.000% coupon and settle June 15. The 3-year, 10-year and 30-year issues produce $119 billion of gross coupon settlement that day, immediately before the June 16-17 FOMC meeting. The long-bond sale will test whether investors require a renewed concession after CPI, PPI and the ECB decision, particularly with the 30-year yield hovering around 5%.

The BOJ decision on June 16 is the principal Asian duration event. A 25-basis-point increase to around 1% is overwhelmingly expected; guidance on a second increase and the pace of bond-purchase reductions will matter more than the first move alone. A clear commitment to further normalization would support the market’s 1.25% year-end rate expectation, while a slower purchase taper could temper JGB volatility but raise questions about the consistency of the tightening signal.

Bank Indonesia’s scheduled June 18 meeting will test whether the off-cycle increase was a stand-alone intervention or the first part of a larger defense. Analysts have raised the possibility of another 50-basis-point move. The decisive evidence will be whether the rupiah’s rebound persists and whether government-bond yields stabilize; further tightening without improvement in duration would reinforce the judgment that institutional and fiscal concerns, rather than insufficient carry alone, are driving foreign retrenchment.

section_summaries.summary: Lower oil and pre-CPI caution pulled Treasury yields down across maturities, with declines in both the 10-year real yield and breakeven inflation. The curve changed little, while higher yields over the past month and persistent Fed hike pricing showed that the strong-employment repricing remained intact. The 3-year auction absorbed supply cleanly, but weaker technology shares and forceful Asian policy responses kept the broader close cautious.

section_summaries.market_read: A 10-year yield near 4.5% restrains borrowing without an immediate policy increase, but investors question whether that is enough.
section_summaries.section_title: Oil Relief Interrupts the Treasury Repricing
section_summaries.summary: The oil retreat delivered an inflation reprieve and helped reverse the previous session's Treasury selloff, but the larger one-month move still reflected higher expected real rates rather than unanchored long-term inflation. Strong employment, AI-related investment and concentrated bearish rate positions preserved sensitivity to CPI even as cash yields declined.

section_summaries.market_read: Strong demand can ease immediate supply pressure without resolving the policy outlook or demand for longer-duration risk.
section_summaries.section_title: Auction Demand Holds as Hike Hedges Build
section_summaries.summary: The $58 billion 3-year auction cleared at 4.192% with a stronger 2.64 bid-to-cover ratio and broader direct and indirect participation, showing demand at repriced yields without weakening expectations for Fed increases. Corporate financing remained sharply segmented: Tencent attracted strong cross-currency demand, Vedanta pursued cheaper refinancing, and Shutterfly offered a 12% yield plus tighter creditor protections.

section_summaries.market_read: Higher policy rates can support currencies, but sovereign duration still reflects liquidity, fiscal and institutional risk.
section_summaries.section_title: Asian Markets Test the Limits of Monetary Defense
section_summaries.summary: Bank Indonesia's unscheduled 25-basis-point increase lifted the rupiah but did not stop government bonds from selling off as fiscal policy and central-bank independence remained in focus. Taiwan's bond selloff combined tight cash with expected tightening, while Japan's debate shifted from an anticipated June increase toward a second move and the future pace of bond-purchase reductions.

section_summaries.section_title: European Growth and Credit Stress Complicate Tightening
section_summaries.summary: German production rose only because construction offset flat core manufacturing and weaker autos, while France prepared to raise its inflation forecast and lower growth expectations after the oil shock. That mix complicated expected ECB tightening. Distress also deepened among leveraged European fiber networks, and Senegal remained dependent on progress toward a new IMF program to ease acute financing pressure.

May CPI will test whether inflation pressure remains concentrated in energy or is broadening through core prices, after which 10-year and 30-year Treasury reopenings will measure demand for duration. ECB guidance, BOJ normalization and Bank Indonesia's follow-through will show how far major and emerging-market central banks intend to carry their tightening responses.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally as retreating oil interrupts the post-payroll repricing
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied on June 9 after Iran and Israel halted their latest exchange of strikes, sending WTI down 3.40% to $88.20 and Brent down 2.97% to $91.45. The 2-year yield fell 4.5 basis points to 4.119%, the 10-year declined 4.6 basis points to 4.518% and the 30-year eased 3.9 basis points to 4.998%. Both the 10-year real yield and breakeven inflation fell, showing that lower oil and reduced real-rate compensation contributed to the move.

The rally interrupted rather than reversed the repricing after strong May employment data. Futures still priced a full 25-basis-point Fed increase by year-end, while options targeted one or possibly two increases by mid-September. May CPI on June 10 will test whether softer energy pressure is containing inflation or whether resilient demand is broadening price gains.

Treasury's $58 billion 3-year auction drew stronger participation than the May sale despite clearing at 4.192%, with the bid-to-cover ratio rising to 2.64 and dealers taking only 15.28%. Risk assets remained restrained as technology shares led equities lower and volatility rose, although investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt funds finished modestly higher. In Asia, Indonesia's unscheduled rate increase supported the rupiah but failed to stop a sovereign-bond selloff, underscoring that higher carry alone did not resolve fiscal and institutional concerns.
